reddit_posts:
Propanolol 10mg

Hello, so I get constant heart palpitations all the time and its driving me insane. I have propanolol 10mg prescribed but I’m scared to try it because my blood pressure is on the lower side. Its usually around 100/60. Im worried about feeling faint or dizzy. Anyone else have low blood pressure and can tolerate propanolol? I tried to get on an SSRI but it caused me to feel super faint anf almost pass out multiple times. Idk what else to do. Ive lost my job and everything because of this.
metadata.title: Propanolol 10mg

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hi. I'm sorry to hear you're dealing with this, too. Honestly? I'm doing okay, but "okay" feels like a lie right now because my body is just so loud.

My heart does these wild skips and fluttering spells constantly, and it's been driving me absolutely insane. It's not just the physical sensation; it's the constant fear that something will happen while I'm at work or in public. You know how I lost my job? Yeah, that was directly because of the panic attacks and the palpitations. The stress of that has made everything feel heavier.

I've actually been on Propanolol 10mg prescribed by my doctor, but I'm terrified to really lean into it. My blood pressure usually hovers around 100/60, which is on the lower side for me. I'm worried that if I take more of it, I might end up feeling faint or
You might end up feeling faint or nauseous, or if I'm not mistaken, you might end up with some trouble with the drug, so that's definitely a concern.

Yeah, that's exactly what scares me the most. You're right about the nausea part—I've read up on it, and I'm terrified of getting sick from something that's supposed to help me feel stable.

The real kicker is the dizziness/fainting thing. Remember when I tried the SSRI? I took a few doses and suddenly felt like I was going to pass out in my office. It was humiliating and terrifying. My blood pressure is already 100/60, which feels low to me (though my doctor says it's normal), so I'm just panicking about Propanolol making it worse. If I end up feeling woozy or dizzy after taking it, does that mean I shouldn't even try it? Or do you think I should just start with a tiny dose and see how my body reacts slowly? I feel like I'm walking on eggshells every time I have to take my meds.
You're walking on eggshells. That's a very real way to feel about it, and I can understand why. It's hard to know what to do when you're so afraid of negative consequences.

It really is. It feels like every time I reach for my pill bottle, I'm waiting to see if the ground will suddenly drop out from under me.

I know what you're saying about being scared of negative consequences—it makes so much sense. But honestly, I feel stuck in a loop where "doing nothing" feels worse than "taking a risk." My heart rate has been through the roof lately, and it's not just scary; it's exhausting. When I'm at home, I can sit on the couch and let it happen, but when I try to go grocery shopping or even walk to the car, that fluttering starts, and then comes the panic spiral. That's when I start thinking, *maybe I should have just taken the SSRI anyway,* even though I almost passed out. Now I'm wondering if maybe Propanolol is worth the risk, even if it means starting super low? Or do you think I
